title: Grateful Dead Live at Academy of Music on 1972-03-22
lineage: Dat (Sony D8) -> Samplitude Professional v9.11 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Apogee AD500 -> Dat (48k)

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with good transfer despite vocal‑mic and drum mix quirks; the show shines with a monster Caution → Uncle John’s jam, stellar Mr. Charlie and a soaring China Cat > Rider.
ai_review.review: The Miller SBD captures a historically important March ’72 Academy of Music run. While the vocal mics sit forward and the drums are a bit hot, the overall transfer is clean enough to enjoy the transcendent jams – especially the beautiful Caution‑UJB segue, the fiery Mr. Charlie, and the tight China Cat Sunflower / I Know You Rider. The performance is high‑energy with a few first‑set hiccups but many standout moments.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is consistently praised (many 5‑star comments) while recording quality has notable mix issues; weighted average yields a strong 4.2 rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clean Miller transfer, but vocal mics are overly prominent and drums sit too loud; occasional monitor buzz and early‑set dropouts noted.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
Sugar Magnolia > Caution > Uncle John's Band (jam)
poor_songs: Deal (early version runs off the rails)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Long two‑hour sets with early technical hiccups; first set recovers after a rough start, second set delivers extended jams and smooth segues.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar shines on Mr. Charlie and he experiments with a volume pedal during the RR Blues segment; overall strong lead work.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith contributes organ/piano textures, especially in the beautiful jam leading into Uncle John's Band.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming is praised as great and driving, though the drum mix is a bit too forward.
